# Government & Politics

Topics on the constitutional framework, institutions, elections, and political dynamics of South Korea, from its authoritarian origins to its present democratic republic.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: category-index — maintained by build-structure; do not edit by hand -->
- [Government Structure of South Korea](government-structure.md) — The presidential republic's constitutional framework, its executive, legislative, and judicial branches, and its democratic safeguards.
- [South Korea–North Korea Relations and Inter-Korean Diplomacy](north-korea-relations.md) — Inter-Korean relations from the Korean War armistice through the Sunshine Policy, the 2018 summits, and the nuclear-era security standoff shaping South Korean foreign policy.
- [Technology and Innovation Policy in South Korea](technology-innovation-policy.md) — The developmental-state technology strategy: the K-Semiconductor Strategy, R&D funding and tax incentives, the HBM and AI push, the startup ecosystem, and platform, data, and export-control regulation.
- [Military and Defense Policy](military-defense-policy.md) — The armed forces, conscription, and defense industry; the U.S. alliance, deterrence toward North Korea, OPCON, and the arc from military rule to civilian control.
- [Environmental Policy and Sustainability](environmental-policy.md) — Climate and environmental policy from the Green Growth era through carbon neutrality, the K-ETS carbon market, air pollution and plastic waste, the nuclear-phase-out reversal, and corporate ESG commitments.
- [Electoral System and the National Assembly](electoral-system.md) — Presidential and legislative elections, the mixed-member proportional system and 3% threshold, the National Election Commission, entrenched regionalism, and the 2016–2017 and 2024–2025 impeachment crises.
- [Political Parties and Regionalism in South Korea](political-parties-regionalism.md) — The two-bloc party system rooted in the TK–Honam divide; the Democratic and conservative lineages, the 1990 three-party merger and later realignments, regional voting persistence, and the 2024–2025 martial-law crisis and snap election.
- [Korean-Japanese Relations](korean-japanese-relations.md) — The historically fraught, economically interdependent bilateral relationship; the colonial legacy and the comfort-women and forced-labor disputes, the Dokdo territorial claim, the 2019 trade war, and the 2023 reset and Camp David trilateral cooperation.
